q: בת 83 עצמאית בתפקודה ושמורה קוגניטיבית. ברקע סכרת מטופלת ב- METFORMIN עם המוגלובין A1C - 7.5%. מדווחת על בעיות ראיה. פנתה למרפאה עקב הרגשה של הליכה לא יציבה. מספר פעמים מעדה במדרגות, ללא חבלות שהצריכו טיפול רפואי. בבדיקה- ההליכה יציבה על בסיס צר. החולה השלימה מבחן TIMED UP AND GO במשך 16 שניות. בבדיקת רופא עיניים נמצא קטרקט בעין ימין ומיופיה. איזו התערבות למניעת נפילות יכולה להתאים למטופלת?
o: התאמת משקפיים מולטיפוקליות
הליכה עם מקל או עם הליכון מחוץ לבית.
איזון סוכר הדוק יותר לפי הנחיות AGS
ניתוח קטרקט
explanation:
Visual impairment can obscure steps and other hazards even when gait looks stable in clinic. **Consider cataract surgery** for the affected eye after ophthalmic assessment. A first-eye surgery trial reported fewer falls.

**A. Multifocal glasses.** The lower near-vision segment can blur ground-level hazards and step edges.
**B. Outdoor cane or walker.** An aid needs individual gait and balance assessment. A 16-second timed test alone cannot select the device.
**C. Tighter glycemic control.** Lowering HbA1c beyond an individualized goal is not the visual fall-prevention intervention indicated here.
**D. Cataract surgery.** It directly addresses the documented visual impairment associated with tripping on stairs.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 264, 637, 639.

q: A 68-year-old man has lower urinary tract symptoms from benign prostatic hyperplasia and erectile dysfunction. He has no cardiovascular contraindication to PDE-5 inhibitors and takes no BPH medication. Which daily PDE-5 inhibitor does Hazzard identify as FDA-approved for male LUTS?
o: Daily tadalafil treatment
Daily sildenafil treatment
Daily vardenafil treatment
Daily avanafil treatment
explanation:
Several PDE5 inhibitors treat erectile dysfunction, but **daily tadalafil** also has a specific indication for male lower urinary tract symptoms associated with BPH.

**A. Daily tadalafil treatment.** Daily tadalafil can address both bothersome BPH symptoms and erectile dysfunction in an appropriate patient.
**B. Daily sildenafil treatment.** Sildenafil shares the mechanism but lacks the specified daily BPH indication.
**C. Daily vardenafil treatment.** Vardenafil is used for erectile dysfunction and is not the agent with this BPH indication.
**D. Daily avanafil treatment.** Avanafil likewise lacks the daily BPH indication asked about.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 567.

q: A 69-year-old woman with coronary disease asks why LDL cholesterol can serve as a treatment-development biomarker whereas developing biomarkers for aging interventions remains difficult. Which explanation matches Hazzard?
o: An established single aging pathway makes the main difference the duration of trials
LDL has a causal atherosclerotic role; no single longevity pathway is identified
Validated aging surrogate endpoints make the main difference the cost of clinical trials
Aging biomarkers need no linkage between treatment-related changes and health outcomes
explanation:
A treatment biomarker is easier to interpret when the biological factor has a causal role in disease. **LDL contributes causally to atherosclerosis, whereas no single pathway explains human longevity**.

**A. One known longevity pathway.** Aging reflects interacting processes and cannot be reduced to one established pathway.
**B. Causal LDL versus complex longevity.** LDL has a defined disease relationship. An aging marker must earn an analogous link to meaningful outcomes.
**C. Validated aging endpoints already exist.** Validation of treatment surrogates is itself a major challenge beyond trial expense.
**D. No outcome link needed.** Treatment-related biomarker change must be linked to altered health risk before substituting for an outcome.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 602.

q: A 79-year-old woman with new atrial fibrillation (CHA2DS2-VASc score 4) and stage 3b chronic kidney disease (eGFR 38) starts amiodarone for rhythm control after unsuccessful metoprolol and diltiazem treatment. Baseline QTc is 438 ms. Two weeks later, she develops tremor and heat intolerance. TSH is 0.02, previously 2.1, and free T4 is 3.8 (reference range 0.8–1.8). Which approach best reflects Hazzard's management of amiodarone-associated thyroid dysfunction?
o: Stop amiodarone and select methimazole before evaluating the thyroid mechanism
Continue amiodarone and select thyroid treatment according to the mechanism
Stop amiodarone and select prednisone before evaluating the thyroid mechanism
Continue amiodarone and defer thyroid treatment until a later laboratory review
explanation:
Amiodarone-associated thyrotoxicosis can reflect increased synthesis or destructive release of stored hormone. **Treat the thyroid disorder according to its mechanism and individualize continuation of amiodarone with the cardiac team**, particularly when it controls a difficult arrhythmia.

**A. Stop and give methimazole immediately.** Thionamides address new synthesis and may be ineffective in purely destructive thyroiditis.
**B. Continue if indicated and choose mechanism-based treatment.** Assess for nodular autonomy, Graves disease or thyroiditis before selecting treatment.
**C. Stop and give prednisone immediately.** Corticosteroids fit destructive thyroiditis. These tests alone cannot distinguish the mechanism.
**D. Continue and defer treatment.** Symptomatic biochemical thyrotoxicosis requires prompt evaluation and management.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1547, 1548.

q: איזו מהתרופות הבאות היא בעלת האפקט האנטי כולינרגי הנמוך ביותר?
o: METOCLOPRAMIDE (PRAMIN)
ESCITALOPRAM (CIPRALEX)
AMITRIPTYLINE (ELATROL)
PROMETHAZINE (PHENERGAN)
explanation:
**Escitalopram has little antimuscarinic activity** and is the preferred answer in this comparison. Assess cognitive and fall risks separately from the anticholinergic burden.

**A. Metoclopramide.** Primarily a dopamine antagonist. Its major neurologic concern is extrapyramidal toxicity, and it also has little direct antimuscarinic action.
**B. Escitalopram.** An SSRI with relatively low anticholinergic burden, especially compared with amitriptyline or promethazine.
**C. Amitriptyline.** This tricyclic is strongly anticholinergic and can cause dry mouth, retention or confusion.
**D. Promethazine.** This first-generation antihistamine is sedating and strongly anticholinergic.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 922, 929–930, 1064. 2023 AGS Beers Criteria, Tables 2 and 7.

Key note: Metoclopramide is chiefly a dopamine antagonist, and the cited references do not give a head-to-head anticholinergic ranking that uniquely separates it from escitalopram.

q: An older adult develops leakage of loose stool after starting over-the-counter products to improve bowel movements. Fecal impaction has been excluded. Which history directly investigates a possible precipitant of the new symptoms?
o: Review alcohol intake patterns from years before the symptoms began
Record the composition of meals in a diary over the coming week
Review new drugs and supplements, including OTC laxatives
Review the history of colorectal cancer among first-degree relatives
explanation:
New loose-stool leakage after starting bowel products suggests a medication or supplement effect. **Identify the recently added OTC laxatives or supplements**, including their doses and timing.

**A. Remote alcohol intake.** The remote history does not address the immediate exposure before symptom onset.
**B. Future food diary.** Diet is relevant, but prospective recording misses the products she just started.
**C. New products.** Excessive laxation can produce liquid stool and overwhelm continence despite an empty rectum.
**D. Family cancer history.** It informs broader risk assessment but cannot explain a temporal drug effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1363.

q: בן 75, לאחר אירוע מוחי ופגיעה בפלג גוף ימין. בבדיקתו: ביד ימין - תנועה כנגד כוח הכבידה ולא כנגד תנגודת. ברגל ימין לא הופקה תנועה כלל. איך מוגדר הכוח בגפיים?
o: רגל 0/5 יד 5/5
רגל 1/5 יד 4/5
רגל 0/5 יד 3/5
רגל 1/5 יד 2/5
explanation:
On the Medical Research Council scale, **leg 0/5 and arm 3/5** matches absent leg movement and an arm that lifts against gravity but yields to resistance. Grade 0 assumes no palpable contraction.

**A. Leg 0/5, arm 5/5.** An arm graded 5 tolerates full resistance.
**B. Leg 1/5, arm 4/5.** Grade 1 requires a detectable contraction, and grade 4 requires some resistance.
**C. Leg 0/5, arm 3/5.** An antigravity movement through range qualifies for grade 3.
**D. Leg 1/5, arm 2/5.** Grade 2 movement requires gravity to be eliminated.

Reference · Medical Research Council, Aids to the Examination of the Peripheral Nervous System, muscle power grading scale.

q: מה מהבאים לא מוכר כסיבוך של האכלת צינור?
o: עצירות
תמותה
דלקת ריאות
ירידה במשקל
explanation:
Enteral feeding supplies nutrition through a tube but can cause gastrointestinal or respiratory complications. It also does not guarantee weight maintenance or survival in a frail patient.

**None of these outcomes can be reliably excluded as a complication.** Constipation is a recognized gastrointestinal problem, and weight loss, aspiration pneumonia and death have been reported among tube-fed patients with pressure injuries.

**A. Constipation.** Enteral nutrition can be accompanied by constipation. Review hydration, fiber intake, medications and bowel function.
**B. Death.** Severe complications of tube feeding can contribute to death. A death in a tube-fed patient requires clinical attribution because underlying illness also influences survival.
**C. Pneumonia.** Aspiration of refluxed feed or secretions can cause pneumonia despite tube access.
**D. Weight loss.** A feeding tube cannot guarantee delivery or absorption of prescribed calories. Weight loss is specifically reported in this clinical population.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 692. ESPEN guideline on home enteral nutrition, monitoring and complications, 2020.
Key note: All four responses received credit. Hazzard lists weight loss, aspiration pneumonia and death, and ESPEN also recognizes constipation. Each can occur with tube feeding.

q:
בן 81, ברקע: אי ספיקת כליות כרונית עם קריאטנין בסיס 2, ischemic cardiomyopathy עם EF של 35%. אושפז בפנימית בשל זיהום בדרכי השתן. יום לאחר אשפוזו המטופל בקוצר נשימה, סטורציה 92% באוויר חדר, לחץ דם- 143/85, דופק 86, שימוש בשרירי עזר. בבדיקה גופנית חרחורים מפושטים לחים, כניסת אוויר מופחתת בבסיסי הריאות. בצילום חזה- בצקת ריאות.
מה הגישה הטיפולית הנכונה?
o: עקב אי ספיקה כלייתית בכדי להגיע לטיפול אפקטיבי יש לטפל במטופל זה ב- FUSID במינון גבוה
טיפול ב- MORPHINE מומלץ היות והראה שיפור פרוגנוסטי בחולים אלה
יש לטפל במסכת חמצן במינימום הנדרש להשגת סטורציה מעל 90% למניעת צבירת CO2
עקב אי ספיקה כלייתית יש להעדיף טיפול משתן ב- DISOTHIASIDE
keySource: IMA 2022-Jun Basic official answer key after appeals, Q133
explanation:
Pulmonary edema in HFrEF requires prompt respiratory support and decongestion. **A higher loop-diuretic dose may be needed with renal insufficiency** to achieve adequate natriuresis.

**A. Higher-dose furosemide.** Reduced drug delivery to the renal tubule can blunt the response. Monitor urine output, renal function and electrolytes.
**B. Morphine improves prognosis.** Relief of distress is different from improved survival. Observational data raise concern for harm.
**C. Restrict oxygen to prevent CO₂ retention.** Titrate oxygen to hypoxemia and assess ventilatory needs. No chronic hypercapnic disorder is stated.
**D. Prefer a thiazide.** Loop diuretics are first-line for significant congestion. A thiazide can augment inadequate loop response.

Reference · Harrison 22e, pp. 1996, 2330–2331.
